rules.description: Output requested on an input-only GPIO.
rules.detection_condition: Constant GPIO argument resolves to a pin whose profile entry has input_only = true (GPIO34-39 on ESP32), and the operation drives the pin (pinMode OUTPUT/OPEN_DRAIN, digitalWrite, analogWrite, LEDC attach, gpio_set_direction output, UART TX, I2C SDA/SCL, SPI SCK/MOSI/SS).
rules.explanation: The pin has no output driver. Writing to it has no effect on the hardware, so the circuit will not behave as the code intends.
rules.recommendation: Move the output to a GPIO that supports output (see the profile's gpio table).
limitations: Only constant GPIO arguments are checked.

rules.description: Flash-connected GPIO used as an ordinary GPIO.
rules.detection_condition: Constant GPIO argument resolves to a pin marked flash_connected (GPIO6-11 on ESP32-WROOM-32).
rules.explanation: These pins are wired to the module's SPI flash. Reconfiguring them interferes with code fetch from flash and typically crashes the device.
rules.recommendation: Do not use GPIO6-GPIO11 on ESP32-WROOM-32.
limitations: Applies to the module profile; bare-chip designs may wire flash differently.

rules.description: Strapping pin configured by the application.
rules.detection_condition: Constant GPIO argument is a strapping pin. LOW when it is driven or given a pull resistor (MEDIUM for GPIO12/MTDI, which selects the flash voltage), INFO when only read.
rules.explanation: Strapping pins are sampled at reset. Using them after boot is allowed; the risk is external circuitry that holds the pin at a non-default level while the chip resets.
rules.recommendation: Make sure the attached circuit leaves the pin at its default level during reset, or use a non-strapping GPIO.
limitations: ShipSafe cannot see the schematic; it only knows how the firmware uses the pin.

rules.description: GPIO number does not exist on the selected chip.
rules.detection_condition: Constant GPIO argument is not in the profile's valid_gpio_numbers.
rules.explanation: There is no such GPIO; the call fails or acts on nothing.
rules.recommendation: Use a GPIO number that exists on the selected chip.

rules.description: GPIO exists on the chip but is not a pin of the selected module.
rules.detection_condition: Constant GPIO argument has exposed_on_module = false (GPIO37/GPIO38 on ESP32-WROOM-32).
rules.explanation: The signal cannot be connected to anything outside the module.
rules.recommendation: Use a GPIO that is a module pin.

rules.description: Peripheral function not supported on this GPIO.
rules.detection_condition: The operation needs an ADC, DAC or touch channel and the profile lists none for this GPIO.
rules.explanation: Only specific GPIOs are connected to the ADC, DAC and touch sensor (datasheet Table 2 and Table 11).
rules.recommendation: Use a GPIO that provides the required analog function.

rules.description: Internal pull resistor requested on a GPIO that has none.
rules.detection_condition: Constant GPIO argument has internal_pull_resistors = false (GPIO34-39).
rules.explanation: GPIO34-39 have no software-enabled pull-up or pull-down; the input floats unless an external resistor is fitted.
rules.recommendation: Add an external pull resistor or use another GPIO.
limitations: An external resistor on the board is not visible to ShipSafe.

rules.description: ADC2 pin read in a project that uses Wi-Fi.
rules.detection_condition: Constant GPIO argument is an ADC2 channel and the project calls Wi-Fi APIs anywhere.
required_context: Wi-Fi usage detected in project code
rules.explanation: ADC2 pins cannot be used when Wi-Fi is used (ESP-IDF). Readings fail while Wi-Fi is active.
rules.recommendation: Use an ADC1 pin (GPIO32-39) for analog input in Wi-Fi projects.
limitations: ShipSafe does not know whether Wi-Fi is active at the moment of the read.

rules.description: UART0 console pin reused as GPIO.
rules.detection_condition: GPIO1 (U0TXD) or GPIO3 (U0RXD) is configured by a GPIO API. LOW when the project also uses Serial (UART0), INFO otherwise.
rules.explanation: TXD and RXD are used for flashing and serial logging; reusing them conflicts with Serial output and can disturb programming.
rules.recommendation: Use another GPIO, or stop using Serial on UART0.

rules.detection_condition: Constant GPIO argument is a JTAG signal pin (MTDI, MTCK, MTMS, MTDO). Reported once per pin.
rules.explanation: External JTAG debugging cannot use the pin while the firmware uses it. This is not evidence that a debug interface is exposed.
rules.recommendation: No action unless you rely on JTAG debugging.

rules.description: Selected chip profile does not match the board in platformio.ini.
rules.detection_condition: The PlatformIO board's MCU (from the registry board list) differs from the MCU the profile describes.
rules.explanation: GPIO capabilities differ between ESP32 family members; results for the wrong profile may be wrong in both directions.
rules.recommendation: Select the chip profile that matches the board, or correct the board in platformio.ini.
limitations: Boards not in the registry board list cannot be checked.

rules.description: GPIO argument is not a compile-time constant; it was not checked.
rules.detection_condition: Clang could not constant-fold the GPIO argument (variable, function result, runtime input).
rules.explanation: The pin number is decided at run time, so ShipSafe reports it as unresolved instead of guessing valid or invalid.
rules.recommendation: Use constexpr/const pin definitions to make hardware checks possible.
limitations: No data-flow analysis is performed to find the value.

rules.explanation: ESP-IDF advises not to use the interrupt of GPIO36 and GPIO39 when using ADC or Wi-Fi and Bluetooth with sleep mode enabled (ESP32 errata GPIO-3.11).
rules.recommendation: Use another GPIO for interrupts, or confirm the errata conditions do not apply.
